source.title: Buckling of Thin-Walled Circular Cylinders
source.author: Mark W. Hilburger
source.locator: Section 4.1, pp.22–23, equations 1–5 and 7; gamma=1 theoretical interpretation explicitly stated below eq.8

quantity: Minimum ideal elastic axial line load Nx for a simply supported unstiffened isotropic circular cylinder; gamma=1. No empirical design-factor or experimental-collapse comparison.
input_basis: Builder-selected dimensional instantiation of the source equations; no published test specimen claimed.
load: Uniform axial compressive edge traction on upper rim; lower axial displacement fixed. No pressure or prestress.
boundary_conditions: Simply supported edges: radial displacement zero at both rims, circumferential displacement zero at rims, free shell rotations; bottom axial displacement zero, top axial edge load uniform. Lateral edge displacement restrains Poisson expansion only at the ends, as explicitly modelled.
element: Gmsh transfinite full cylinder, CalculiX S8R shells, exact radial normals
mesh_convergence_rule: Three frozen meshes; both adjacent abs(N_new-N_old)/abs(N_new)<=0.01. Inspect all modes; do not discard lower modes.
thread_choice_basis: Fixed-deck sphere experiment, committed at 592611e789cbe96c6c43c0cbb78e9ebf0ff66467, found 1/2-thread agreement and 4/8-thread disagreement; choose one thread before this independent case first solve.
load_discretization: Exact circular rim arc length per element, consistent quadratic edge weights (1/6,2/3,1/6) applied in global -z; enforce total force=-2*pi*r*Nref.
comparator_search: m=1..100,n=0..100; minimum no lower than the exact continuous asymptote and within 0.000076% of it
